1: Paul is astonished that the Galatians are turning to a different gospel. Even if an angel preached something contrary, it should be rejected. His own Gospel came by revelation from Christ, who called him when he was persecuting the Church.
The faith is received, not invented or edited. Paul's own conversion shows it came from God.
2: In Jerusalem the leading apostles recognised Paul's mission to the Gentiles. Later, at Antioch, Paul opposed Peter to his face for drawing back from eating with Gentile Christians. A person is made right with God by faith in Christ, not by works of the Law.
Peter's fault was in conduct, not in teaching. "It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me."
3: "O foolish Galatians!" They received the Spirit by believing, not by keeping the Law. The Law was a guardian until Christ came. All who are baptised have put on Christ; there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female.
Baptism makes all believers equal as God's children and heirs of the promise.
4: When the time was right, God sent his Son, born of a woman, so that we could be adopted as his children and cry "Abba, Father". Paul pleads with the Galatians not to go back to slavery, and uses Hagar and Sarah as a picture of two covenants.
A Christian relates to God as a child to a father, not as a slave to a master.
5: Freedom and the fruit of the Spirit

Christ set us free, so do not accept the yoke of slavery again. What counts is faith working through love. Freedom is not an excuse for self-indulgence. The works of the flesh are plain; the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.
Real freedom is the ability to love and do good. The Spirit's fruit is the sign that he is at work in us.
6: Gently restore anyone caught in sin. Bear each other's burdens. People reap what they sow, so do not tire of doing good. Paul boasts in nothing but the cross of Christ.
Faith shows in practical care for others. What matters is being a new creation.
